commitResults.messageTitle: feat/Chatbot name changes, Added greet and exit -- End of Level-0
feat/Echo added using While loops -- End of Level-1
feat/Implemented the A-classes extension -- End of Level-3
Add test-ui skill and UI test plan
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds a project-specific Claude Code skill (.claude/skills/test-ui) that
runs the black-box console test cases recorded in test/ui-test-plan.md
against the compiled build, stopping at the first failure and reporting
the actual vs expected output.

Also updates AGENTS.md (which CLAUDE.md imports) with a "Testing after
code changes" section instructing that ui-test-plan.md be kept in sync
and the test-ui skill invoked after any change to console behavior.

Introduces a custom checked exception (WillException) so invalid or
incomplete commands are reported with a specific, friendly message
instead of crashing or being silently added as garbage data.

Handles: empty todo description, unknown commands, mark/unmark with a
missing/non-numeric/out-of-range task number, and deadline/event missing
their description or /by /from /to clauses.

Updated test/ui-test-plan.md with TC10-TC16 covering these error cases;
all 16 test cases pass via the test-ui skill.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add interleaved edge-case tests to the UI test plan
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds TC17-TC23: tests that interleave valid and invalid commands and
re-check list/state afterwards, e.g. confirming a rejected command
doesn't add a phantom task, mark 0 / mark -1 are rejected as
out-of-range rather than off-by-one, whitespace inside a description is
preserved, deadline/event with an empty description before /by or
/from is rejected, and unmark on an already-not-done task is idempotent.

Verified the test-ui skill actually catches regressions: temporarily
removed the deadline empty-description check, reran the suite, and
confirmed TC21 failed with a clear expected-vs-actual diff before
reverting the bug.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add delete command; switch task storage to ArrayList<Task>
commitResults.messageBody:
Implements the A-Collections extension: replaces the fixed-size Task[]
with an ArrayList<Task> for dynamic sizing and simpler add/remove.

Adds a `delete <task number>` command that removes the task at that
position, echoes it back ("Noted. I've removed this task:"), and
reports the new task count. Reuses the existing parseTaskIndex
validation (now parameterized by command name so mark/unmark/delete
each get an accurate usage hint on error).

Updated test/ui-test-plan.md with TC24-26 covering delete (success,
missing argument, out-of-range), and fixed TC11's expected wording for
the unknown-command message, which now lists "delete" as a valid
command. All 26 test cases pass via the test-ui skill.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add TaskType enum for the A-Enums extension
commitResults.messageBody:
Replaces the hardcoded "[T]"/"[D]"/"[E]" string literals duplicated in
each of Todo/Deadline/Event's toString() override with a single
TaskType enum (TODO, DEADLINE, EVENT), each carrying its display
symbol. Task now stores its TaskType and owns the full
"[tag][status] description" formatting, so subclasses only append
their own extra details (by/from/to) instead of re-deriving the tag.

Behavior-preserving: rebuilt and reran the full test-ui suite (26/26
still pass) to confirm the list/mark/unmark/delete output is unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Redesign/README.md changes for suitable chatbot name
Save tasks to disk on every change
Load tasks from disk at startup
Fix crash and data-corruption bugs, harden input parsing
Add on <date>' to find tasks on a specific date
Extract Ui class out of Will
commitResults.messageBody:
A-MoreOOP increment 1/4: pull the user-interaction concerns out of the
Will monolith into a new Ui class.

Ui now owns:
- showWelcome(): the startup banner + greeting, previously inline at
  the top of main().
- showGoodbye(): the farewell message shown on "bye".
- showLine() / showMessage(): the divider and indented-message framing
  used by every command branch, previously static helpers on Will.

Will now holds a single Ui instance (created once in main()) and
routes every print through it, including the two warning messages
inside loadTasks(), which now takes the Ui as a parameter since it is
a static helper invoked before the command loop exists.

This is a pure refactor: no user-visible behavior changed. Verified
against the full ui-test-plan.md suite (42/42 automated cases still
pass) before committing.

Why extract Ui first, before Storage/Parser/TaskList: it is the most
self-contained of the four — none of its methods depend on tasks, file
I/O, or command parsing — so it can be pulled out with the least risk
and gives an easy first checkpoint for the rest of the refactor.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract Storage class out of Will
commitResults.messageBody:
A-MoreOOP increment 2/4: pull the file-persistence concerns out of the
Will monolith into a new Storage class.

Storage now owns:
- load(ui): reads the save file into an ArrayList<Task>, returning an
  empty list on first run (file absent) and skipping+warning on a
  corrupted line rather than aborting the whole load. Still takes Ui
  as a parameter, since these warnings are printed at load time,
  before the rest of the program has anything else to report through.
- save(tasks): writes the task list back to disk, creating the parent
  folder on first run.
- parseSavedTask(line): the pipe-delimited line parser, now private to
  Storage since nothing outside it needs to parse a save-file line.

Will no longer hardcodes the save file path as a static constant;
main() now builds a Storage(Paths.get("data", "will.txt")) once and
calls storage.load(ui) / storage.save(tasks) wherever it used to call
the old static loadTasks()/saveTasks() helpers.

Pure refactor: no user-visible behavior changed. Verified against the
full ui-test-plan.md suite (42/42 automated cases still pass,
including the save/load-specific TC27-TC30) before committing.

Why Storage next: TaskList (the next increment) needs an already-
loaded ArrayList<Task> to wrap, and the target constructor shape from
the assignment builds Storage before TaskList for exactly that reason.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract TaskList class out of Will
commitResults.messageBody:
A-MoreOOP increment 3/4: wrap the ArrayList<Task> in a new TaskList
class, matching the target constructor shape (new TaskList(storage
.load(ui))).

TaskList owns:
- add(task) / remove(index) / get(index) / size(): the same
  operations Will was already calling directly on the ArrayList.
- getTasks(): exposes the underlying ArrayList for Storage#save,
  which still serializes a plain ArrayList<Task> to disk.
- Iterable<Task>: so the existing for-each loops in "list" and
  "on <date>" keep compiling and behaving identically without needing
  to be rewritten around a new iteration API.

Will now declares `TaskList tasks` instead of `ArrayList<Task> tasks`;
every call site (add/remove/get/size, the two for-each loops, and the
six storage.save(...) calls, now storage.save(tasks.getTasks())) needed
only its declared type updated, not its logic.

Pure refactor: no user-visible behavior changed. Verified against the
full ui-test-plan.md suite (42/42 automated cases still pass) before
committing.

This completes the minimal A-MoreOOP target (Ui, Storage, Parser,
TaskList) except Parser, which is being folded into the stretch-goal
increment next: introducing the Command hierarchy and rewriting Parser
to return Command objects, then rewiring Will.run() to the loop shape
from the stretch goal instead of the if/else dispatch.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Command hierarchy and rewrite Parser (A-MoreOOP stretch goal)
commitResults.messageBody:
A-MoreOOP increment 4/4: introduce an abstract Command class and one
concrete subclass per command, rewrite Parser to return Command
objects instead of executing them inline, and rewire Will around the
run() loop shape from the stretch goal.

New classes:
- Command (abstract): execute(tasks, ui, storage) + isExit(), plus a
  shared requireValidIndex(tasks, index) helper for mark/unmark/delete.
- ExitCommand, ListCommand, OnCommand, MarkCommand, UnmarkCommand,
  DeleteCommand: one class per command, each holding just the
  arguments it needs (e.g. OnCommand holds the parsed LocalDate,
  Mark/Unmark/Delete hold the task index).
- AddCommand: one class for todo/deadline/event, since all three only
  differ in which Task subclass Parser constructs before wrapping it.

Parser now has parse(String) -> Command, replacing the if/else chain
that used to live directly in Will's main loop. One real design
consequence: Parser only sees raw text, not the TaskList, so it can no
longer bounds-check a mark/unmark/delete task number against the
current list size the way the old inline code did. That check moved
into Command#requireValidIndex, called at the start of each of those
three commands' execute() — without it, an out-of-range index would
throw an uncaught IndexOutOfBoundsException instead of a graceful
WillException.

Will is now instance-based: a Will(filePath) constructor builds
ui/storage/tasks and prints the welcome+load sequence, and run() is
just the loop: read a line, Parser.parse it, execute the Command,
check isExit(). main() is a one-liner. This finishes the assignment's
suggested target shape (Duke(filePath) + run() + one-line main()).

Two deliberate deviations from the stretch goal's literal sample code,
both made to keep this a zero-behavior-change refactor:

1. The sample calls ui.showLine() both right after ui.readCommand()
   and again in the finally block. Tracing that through: every
   iteration after the first would print a divider immediately after
   reading input (closing the previous response) AND another divider
   right after via finally (closing this response) with nothing
   printed between them - two consecutive divider lines where the
   current output (and all 43 existing test cases) expects exactly
   one shared divider between responses. I kept a single ui.showLine()
   per iteration, in finally only, which reproduces the current
   divider placement exactly.

2. The sample's Duke(filePath) constructor wraps storage.load() in a
   try/catch and falls back to an empty TaskList with
   ui.showLoadingError() on any failure. Storage#load already handles
   this differently (skip a corrupted line with a warning, keep
   loading the rest) - a deliberate design from A-Storage that TC30
   specifically tests. Switching to all-or-nothing loading would be a
   real behavior change, not a refactor, so I kept load(ui)'s current
   signature and per-line-tolerant behavior.

Caught one bug via the test suite before this was even a candidate
commit: my first pass called storage.load(ui) inside the constructor
before ui.showWelcome(), which printed a corrupted-line warning before
the banner instead of after it (TC30 failed). Fixed by keeping the
constructor's order as showWelcome() then load(), matching the
original sequence.

Verified against the full ui-test-plan.md suite: 42/42 automated cases
pass, with byte-for-byte identical output to before this increment.

This completes A-MoreOOP, including the stretch goal. Next step is
merging branch-A-MoreOOP into master (--no-ff), tagging it, and moving
on to A-Packages.

commitResults.messageTitle: Organize classes into will / will.task / will.command packages
commitResults.messageBody:
A-Packages: keep src/main/java as the source root, move every class
out of the default package into one of three packages, grouped by
responsibility (going straight for the stretch goal rather than the
minimal single-package option, since 20 classes in one flat package
was already past the point where a split pays off):

- will (root): Will, Ui, Storage, Parser, TaskList, WillException -
  the "wiring" classes, each talking to several of the others, so
  none of them fit more specifically into task/ or command/.
- will.task: Task, TaskType, Todo, Deadline, Event, FlexibleDate -
  what a task is. FlexibleDate lives here since it's exclusively used
  by task date fields and date-matching.
- will.command: Command, ExitCommand, ListCommand, OnCommand,
  MarkCommand, UnmarkCommand, DeleteCommand, AddCommand - what a
  command does.

This mirrors the course's own worked example (duke.task, duke.command)
fairly closely. WillException stays in the root package rather than
getting its own package, since it's thrown/caught from all three
groups and a package for one class felt like more ceremony than
benefit at this size; TaskList stays in root rather than will.task
since the assignment explicitly pairs it with Will/Ui/Storage/Parser
as a sibling, not a "what is a task" class.

Pure move: only package declarations and the imports needed to reach
classes now in a different package changed - no logic changed. Updated
the build/run commands in ui-test-plan.md (recursive javac instead of
the old flat src/main/java/*.java wildcard, and `java -cp out will.Will`
instead of `java -cp out Will`) and run_tests.py's harness to match.

Verified against the full ui-test-plan.md suite after moving: 42/42
automated cases pass, with zero output changes.

A-Gradle step 1: bring in the course-provided Gradle setup (build.gradle,
the Gradle wrapper jar/properties, gradlew, gradlew.bat) from the
add-gradle-support branch in the fork.

That branch forked from an old point in this project's history (before
Duke.java was renamed to Will.java, before tasks/save-load/dates/
A-MoreOOP/A-Packages), so relative to the actual merge base it only
adds those 5 Gradle files - it doesn't touch any of the Java sources.
One conflict came from that age gap: add-gradle-support still carries
the original Duke.java unchanged, while master deleted it back when
the chatbot was renamed. Resolved by keeping the deletion, since
add-gradle-support never intentionally modified that file - it just
predates the rename.

Note for the next step: build.gradle's `application { mainClass = ... }`
still points at the placeholder 'seedu.duke.Duke', which doesn't exist
in this project under any name. That'll need updating to the real
entry point before `gradle run` works - not done here, since this
commit is just step 1 (merge the branch in), and the answer depends on
whether branch-A-Packages is merged into master first (Will vs
will.Will).

commitResults.messageTitle: Point build.gradle at the real entry point and jar name
commitResults.messageBody:
A-Gradle step 1 (minimal target): after merging the add-gradle-support
branch in, build.gradle still had two placeholders left over from the
course template that don't match this project at all:

- application.mainClass was 'seedu.duke.Duke', which doesn't exist
  under any name here (the chatbot was renamed to Will long ago, and
  A-Packages moved it into the will package) - `gradle run` could not
  have worked until this pointed at the real entry point, will.Will.
- shadowJar's archiveFileName was 'duke.jar'; renamed to 'will.jar' to
  match, for the same reason the banner/README were already renamed.

Verified locally: built a scratch build.gradle with just the
java+application plugins (skipping the shadow plugin, since resolving
it hit a network restriction in my sandbox unrelated to this fix) and
ran `gradle run` with mainClass = 'will.Will' - it launched the
program, printed the full welcome banner, and handled `bye` cleanly.
The shadow-plugin resolution itself should be tried on a machine with
normal internet access (this repo's actual build.gradle, restored
after the scratch test, is unchanged apart from the two fixes above).

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JUnit tests for FlexibleDate, Task, and Deadline
commitResults.messageBody:
Covers the A-JUnit minimal target (two non-trivial methods from two
different classes) and beyond: FlexibleDateTest (9 tests), TaskTest
(8 tests, via Todo), and DeadlineTest (6 tests) covering the
polymorphic overrides. 23 tests total under src/test/java, mirroring
the will.task package layout. Documented in ui-test-plan.md.

build.gradle needed no changes: the shadowJar plugin, application
plugin, and shadowJar { archiveFileName = 'will.jar' } were already
wired up in A-Gradle. /build/ is already gitignored, so the built
JAR is never committed, consistent with distributing it via a GitHub
release instead. Documents how to create, locate, and run the JAR.

Current situation: an AI Guidance-prompted audit against the SE-EDU
Java coding standard (see the new seedu-java-coding-standard skill)
found a small number of concrete violations in the existing code.

What's being done:
* Reorder OnCommand's imports (FlexibleDate before Task) to fix the
  only import-ordering violation found.
* Add the required class-level Javadoc to Task, Todo, Deadline, and
  Event, which had none.
* Add the required method Javadoc to Parser#parse(), plus brief
  Javadoc to the Storage and Will constructors, Will#run(), and
  Will#main(), which the standard also requires for public methods.

Why: header comments are required for all public classes/methods
under the standard, and import order must be consistent; these four
classes and this one method were the only gaps. No behavior changes —
this is comments and import order only, so the full test suite
(manual UI tests and JUnit) is unaffected.

Current situation: the project follows the SE-EDU Java coding
standard (per the previous commit's fixes), but that standard wasn't
written down anywhere an AI assistant (or a person) working on this
repo could look it up.

What's being done: add a project-specific skill,
.claude/skills/seedu-java-coding-standard/SKILL.md, summarizing the
naming, formatting, code-organization, and comment rules from
https://se-education.org/guides/conventions/java/intermediate.html,
and mandate it in AGENTS.md for all Java code in this project.

Why: so the standard is consulted automatically before writing new
code and when reviewing existing code, instead of relying on it being
remembered.

Current situation: AGENTS.md already had the course's Git conventions
written out inline (subject/body format, branch naming), but as free
text rather than a skill an assistant is directed to consult and
apply consistently.

What's being done: add a project-specific skill,
.claude/skills/seedu-git-standard/SKILL.md, based on
https://se-education.org/guides/conventions/git.html, and replace the
inline rules in AGENTS.md's Git section with a mandate to follow that
skill for every future commit and branch name.

Why: keeps the convention in one place instead of duplicated across
AGENTS.md and memory, and makes it something explicitly invoked before
each commit rather than passively stated.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JavaDoc to all non-private classes and methods
commitResults.messageBody:
Current situation: several public classes (Task, Todo, Deadline,
Event) had no class-level header comment, and many public
methods/constructors across Parser, Storage, TaskList, Will,
WillException, the Command subclasses, and the Task hierarchy had
none either.

What's being done: add header comments to every non-private class and
method, and to the non-trivial private parsing helpers in Parser,
meeting the A-JavaDoc stretch goal. Overrides whose behavior is
already described by the class-level Javadoc or the abstract method
they implement (e.g. each Command's execute()) are left to inherit
that documentation rather than repeating it. Also fixes the same
OnCommand import-order slip independently found during the pass.

Why: header comments are required for public classes/methods so
anyone reading the Javadoc (not just the source) can understand the
API; this was the only gap in an otherwise-typical class per the
standard.

Both branch-A-CodingStandard and the just-merged branch-A-JavaDoc
touched several of the same files (Task, Todo, Deadline, Event,
Parser, Storage, Will, OnCommand), independently adding overlapping
Javadoc and the same OnCommand import-order fix. Since A-JavaDoc's
pass was a superset of A-CodingStandard's changes to those files, this
merge resolves cleanly with no net change to them; the new content
from this branch is AGENTS.md's coding-standard/git-standard mandates
and the two new project-specific skills.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add find <keyword> to search tasks by description
commitResults.messageBody:
Current situation: there was no way to look up a task by its
description text — only list, or query by date via on.

What's being done: add a FindCommand (mirroring OnCommand's shape)
that lists every task whose description contains the given keyword,
case-insensitively, renumbered within the filtered results. Parser
gains a find branch and a parseFind helper that rejects a missing
keyword. Adds TC44-TC47 to ui-test-plan.md covering matches across
task types, case-insensitivity, no matches, and no keyword.

Why: case-insensitive substring match is the most forgiving default
for a quick keyword search, and keeps the implementation consistent
with the existing on-command's filter-and-renumber pattern rather
than introducing a new approach.

branch-Level-9 and the already-merged branch-A-JavaDoc both touched
Parser.java and test/ui-test-plan.md (Javadoc additions vs. the new
find command), but at non-overlapping locations in each file, so this
merges cleanly with no lost content from either side.
